source.title: Dopaminergic neurons promote hippocampal reactivation and spatial memory persistence

confidence_rationale: Causal optogenetic evidence that midbrain dopaminergic input to hippocampus enhances place-cell assembly reactivation and stabilizes spatial memory at newly learned goal locations -- directly supporting the 'stability / durability' sub-component of MECH-232's representational-expansion claim. Held below the Krishnan entry because it targets reactivation/persistence (the stability leg) rather than density/over-representation, and does not address the implicit-vs-explicit-gradient CRUX at all.
failure_signatures: Demonstrates DA-driven stabilization of goal-location representations but says nothing about whether that stability substitutes for, or is distinct from, an explicit positive-valence tag -- the MECH-232 dissociation is untested.

Effect is on offline reactivation during sleep/rest and subsequent recall; MECH-232 as instantiated in REE is an online CEM-scoring / terrain mechanism, so the mapping crosses a consolidation-vs-online-planning boundary.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Optogenetic burst stimulation of hippocampal dopaminergic fibers from midbrain neurons, delivered while mice explored novel environments, enhanced reactivation of CA1 pyramidal-cell assemblies during subsequent sleep/rest. Delivered during learning of new goal locations, it improved later recall of spatial neural representations and stabilized memory performance.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the 'stability / durability' facet of MECH-232's representational-expansion account: dopamine at reward/goal-relevant locations makes those hippocampal representations more durable and more easily reactivated, i.e. it upgrades representational quality rather than adding a valence field. Corresponds to the place-field stability leg of the SD-024 substrate readouts (V3-EXQ-766 leg-1 'stability' supporting metric).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Evidence is about offline reactivation and memory persistence, not online density/over-representation or approach behaviour. It reinforces one facet (stability/durability) of the representational-expansion claim and is orthogonal to the implicit-vs-explicit-gradient CRUX. Rodent optogenetics -> REE abstract terrain transfer by functional analogy.
mapping.source_context: Male transgenic (TH-Cre) mice, freely moving, appetitive spatial goal-learning task; optogenetic burst stimulation of midbrain dopaminergic fibers in dorsal hippocampus; CA1 assembly recording across sleep/rest.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality causal optogenetic study, strong venue. Mapping fidelity moderate: it evidences the stability/durability facet but not density/over-representation or the approach dissociation, and lives on the consolidation timescale rather than REE's online CEM terrain. Transfer risk moderate-to-high for the same online-vs-offline reason.
